newsitem.title: USA: CoCensys drug is well-tolerated in test.
newsitem.headline: CoCensys drug is well-tolerated in test.

text.p: CoCensys Inc said on Tuesday it plans to present test data suggesting its drug CCD 1042, an anticonvulsant also called ganaxolone, is well tolerated and may have an antiepileptic effect in children with uncontrolled epilepsy.
The company said it plans to present information from Phase II clinical trials at the American Epilepsy Society meeting in San Francisco.
The trial, completed earlier this year in France, included 15 patients aged five to 15 years-old who were not responding to treatment with currently available anti-epileptic drugs.
In the open-label trials, six patients showed a clinically relevant -- over 50 percent -- reduction in seizure frequency when ganaxolone was added to their treatment regimen, it said.

"This trial was designed only to show safety. To see a signal of efficacy in this type of patient population, which responds very poorly to established anti-eplieptic drugs, is encouraging," David A.H. Lee, executive vice president of research and development, said in a statement.
CoCensys is conducting another pilot Phase II study in the United States, which includes children two months to five years-old with epilepsy refractory to other treatments.

The data to be announced today by ConCensys showed the most frequently reported side-effect of ganaxolone was sedation, which was predicted from the drug's pharmacological action. Blood levels of other antiepileptic medications these patients were taking showed no evidence of altered metabolism after escalating doses of ganaxolone, CoCensys said.
CCD 1042 is a synthetic version of naturally occurring neuroactive steroids, called epalons, that bind to specific receptors in the brain.
